title: Invocation Quality Orchestrator: end-to-end tool selection & argument conformance pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reproducible, automated evaluation pipeline that continuously measures two orthogonal aspects of function/tool invocations across model and config changes: 1) tool selection accuracy (is the model calling the correct tool given the user intent), and 2) argument conformance (are the called args syntactically and semantically valid vs the tool schema). The orchestrator will: 1) subscribe to config/model-change events and spawn evaluation runs, 2) run a diverse corpus (real customer anonymized prompts + synthetic adversarial cases + unit-level schema fuzzers), 3) compute actionable metrics (top-1/top-3 selection accuracy, arg-precision/recall, schema-violation rate, critical-failure rate), 4) snapshot baselines and report regressions vs pinned baselines, 5) gate CI/canary rollouts when thresholds are exceeded, and 6) pipe findings into Console alerts, a PR bot comment, and a RedTeam review queue for high-severity breakages.
acceptance_criteria: Automated runs trigger on model/config change events and queue within 15s
Evaluation corpus covers at least 12 tool schemas, 3 model families, and 4 inference configs (quantized, fp16, batching levels)
Top-1 tool selection accuracy and arg-precision baselines captured; regressions >3% trigger blocking alert
Argument conformance checker flags schema mismatches with examples and suggested fixes in CI comments
Console shows per-route and per-model diffs for invocation metrics, with historical trend for 30 days
CI integration posts a machine-readable summary and a human-facing checklist on pull requests that change routing, tool configs, or model pins
risks_and_mitigations: Data privacy risk: using customer prompts could expose PII. Mitigation: use anonymized, consented dataset + synthetic augmentation and enforce L7 access controls.
Flaky metrics due to sampling variance: Mitigation: seed-based deterministic sampling and statistical significance testing on regression detection.
False positives from schema checker on permissive tool interfaces: Mitigation: maintain schema versions and whitelist compatible field-skips per tool.
CI noise causing rollout delays: Mitigation: two-tier alerts (informational vs blocking) and a human review fast-path for low-risk regressions.
implementation_notes: Harness will be a lightweight orchestration service (k8s job + step function) that reuses existing eval runners
Store artifacts and baselines in S3 bucket s3://redwood-evals/invocation-orch/ with versioned keys
Argument conformance uses JSON Schema + additional semantic validators (type-checking, URI reachable checks, length constraints)
Use Docker image redwood/eval-runner:2026-03 for deterministic runtime; pin seeds inside runners
Expose metrics via Prometheus: invocation_selection_top1, invocation_selection_top3, arg_schema_violation_count, invocation_critical_failure_count
runbook: If a blocking regression is detected, autopause canary rollouts and post to #incidents-invocation-quality

Triage steps: 1) reproduce locally with the exact commit and model snapshot, 2) run adversarial subset to isolate failing patterns, 3) check recent config changes (routing, tool templates, model pin), 4) escalate to model-onboarding and runtime infra if root cause is kernel/quantization related
